must_catch.item: The gaps section shows the rep's 'nothing' being contradicted (PayPal/Venmo, saved cards)
The Braintree theory is labeled opinion
The approval-rate slide is reported as silence in a win
The CFO's one question is surfaced as a messaging signal

fails: Trigger insight states as fact that 'nobody turned it into a business case'. The transcript never says this, and the report's own close lists whether the cost was quantified as unknown.
tag_why and the M2 messaging rationale put 'when' in quotes as if the customer said it ('from bake-off to 'when''). The transcript only says Daniel 'stopped saying "if".'
data.notes: The report gets the core lessons right. It shows the rep's 'clean' claim contradicted by the open Venmo answer and the undelivered saved-card reference, labels the Braintree theory as the rep's guess, and turns the CFO's single question into the 'paid by Friday' messaging signal. Its main flaws are small unsupported embellishments: a definite claim that no business case was built, and a paraphrased 'when' shown as a quote.
